sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗，来自《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I want to thank the American people for the extraordinary honor of being elected your 47th president and your 45th president.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢美国人民，给予我当选你们第47任总统和第45任总统这一无上的荣誉。

sentences.en: In the early hours of Wednesday morning,
sentences.zh: 在周三清晨的早期时刻，

sentences.en: Donald Trump was elected president of the United States for a second time.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普第二次当选美国总统。

sentences.en: This will truly be the golden age of America.
sentences.zh: 这将真正成为美国的黄金时代。

sentences.en: That's what we have done.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所做到的。

sentences.en: Shortly before that call was made, I spoke with three of my colleagues, chief political analyst Nate Cohn, national political correspondent Lisa Lair,
sentences.zh: 在那通电话打完不久前，我与我的三位同事交谈过：首席政治分析师内特·科恩、国家政治记者丽莎·莱尔，

sentences.en: and the host of the run-up podcast,
sentences.zh: 以及播客节目“The Run-Up”的主持人，

sentences.en: Estet Herndon, about how Trump did it.
sentences.zh: 埃斯特·赫恩登，探讨特朗普是如何做到的。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, November 6th.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月6日，星期三。

sentences.en: So Estet, Nate, Lisa, thank you for being here at 1.25 a.m.
sentences.zh: 所以，埃斯特、内特、丽莎，谢谢你们在凌晨1点25分来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我们。

sentences.en: I deeply appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我对此深表感激。

sentences.en: The night's still young for us.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，今夜还很漫长。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But at this moment, it is looking very likely that Donald Trump will be the winner of this election and that he will return to the White House.
sentences.zh: 但此刻，唐纳德·特朗普极有可能是这次选举的胜者，并且他将重返白宫。

sentences.en: So I just want to take a moment and have you all reflect on the significance of that reality, that Trump is now exceedingly likely to have a second term in the White House.
sentences.zh: 所以我只想花点时间，让大家思考一下这一现实的意义——特朗普现在极有可能开启第二任期。

sentences.en: Lisa?
sentences.zh: 丽莎？

sentences.en: Well, this is a huge accomplishment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个巨大的成就。

sentences.en: I mean, I've been thinking about how, in a way,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我一直在想，在某种程度上，

sentences.en: Trump is his own historic firSt.
sentences.zh: 特朗普创造了他自己的历史“第一”。

sentences.en: You know, we talk a lot about barrier-breaking candidates, and Vice President Harris would have been the first female president.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们经常谈论打破壁垒的候选人，而副总统哈里斯本会成为第一位女总统。

sentences.en: Trump, of course, will be the first convicted felon and twice impeached president.
sentences.zh: 当然，特朗普将成为第一位被定罪的重罪犯和曾两度被弹劾的总统。

sentences.en: He'll be the first president in more than 120 years to come back after losing a re-election bid.
sentences.zh: 他将是120多年来第一位在竞选连任失利后卷土重来的总统。

sentences.en: So he is breaking boundaries in his way.
sentences.zh: 所以他正以他自己的方式打破界限。

sentences.en: And, of course, then there's all the things that he promised during the course of his campaign, which really, as we've talked about before on this roundtable,
sentences.zh: 当然，还有他在竞选过程中承诺的所有事情，正如我们在这个圆桌会议上以前讨论过的，

sentences.en: seem to flout, if not directly at, some core principles of the country's founding system of democracy.
sentences.zh: 这些事情似乎公然蔑视了该国建国民主制度的一些核心原则，如果不是直接针对它们的话。

sentences.en: So it does feel like we're headed to a pretty extraordinary and unprecedented second term for Trump and for the nation.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实让人觉得，对于特朗普和国家来说，我们正走向一个相当非凡且前所未有的第二任期。

sentences.en: Is that your reaction?
sentences.zh: 这是你的反应吗？

sentences.en: I think that in 2016, you could have told yourself that America didn't know what it was selecting.
sentences.zh: 我认为在2016年，你还可以对自己说，美国并不知道自己选出了什么。

sentences.en: And I think now you can't, right?
sentences.zh: 而我认为现在你不能这么说了，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, it's not just his literal return.
sentences.zh: 比如，这不仅仅是他的字面回归。

sentences.en: It is the fact that he has been so explicit in the run-up to that return.
sentences.zh: 而是事实在于，他在回归前的言论是如此明确。

sentences.en: The convictions, the sexual assault liability, the, like, you can go on and on and on, but there's not a lack of evidence on who Donald Trump is and what he is promising.
sentences.zh: 定罪、性侵责任，你可以没完没了地列举下去，但对于唐纳德·特朗普是谁以及他承诺了什么，并不缺乏证据。

sentences.en: And so I think that that is the thing that largely sits with me.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这才是最触动我的地方。

sentences.en: And I think on the other side, the Democratic refusal to see the unpopularity of Joe Biden, the dismissal of anyone who talked about a primary, the demanding of party loyalty,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为在另一边，民主党人拒绝正视乔·拜登的不受欢迎程度，对任何谈论初选的人不屑一顾，要求对党绝对忠诚，

sentences.en: all of that looks ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切看起来都十分荒谬。

sentences.en: And the national picture that shows a consistent desire for change, I think has to be read as, first and foremost, a rejection of the current administration.
sentences.zh: 而显示出对变革持续渴望的国家图景，我认为首先必须被解读为对现任政府的否定。

sentences.en: And there was a lot of signs that pointed to that for a long time.
sentences.zh: 而且有大量迹象长期以来都在指向这一点。

sentences.en: And so in the same way I think there is an active embrace of Donald Trump you can ignore,
sentences.zh: 因此，正如我认为你无法忽视对唐纳德·特朗普的积极拥护一样，

sentences.en: I think you also have to point out that the strategy that Democrats took, the self-belief that they had, that they were certain of, has put them in this situation.
sentences.zh: 我认为你也必须指出，民主党采取的战略以及他们深信不疑的自信，将他们置于了这样的境地。

sentences.en: We're going to return to that for sure, Ested, in a little bit.
sentences.zh: 埃斯特，我们等会儿一定会回到这个话题上来。

sentences.en: The soul-searching within the Democratic Party, all the decision-making around Biden.
sentences.zh: 民主党内部的灵魂拷问，所有围绕拜登的决策。

sentences.en: But first, Nate, your quick reaction before we get into the question of how we actually got here tonight.
sentences.zh: 但首先，内特，在你谈及今晚我们是如何走到这一步之前，先谈谈你的简短反应。

sentences.en: Well, Ested took what might have been the gist of mine, so I'll offer a slightly zig where others zagged
sentences.zh: 好的，埃斯特抢去了我原本想说的核心观点，所以我要提供一个稍微反其道而行之的看法，

sentences.en: and reflect on the potentially extraordinary consequences of a second Trump term on almost every major issue
sentences.zh: 并思考特朗普第二任期对几乎所有自二战以来美国达成共识的主大议题所产生的潜在非凡影响，

sentences.en: that there has been consensus on in the United States since World War II, whether it's foreign policy or immigration or trade, norms for constitutional government.
sentences.zh: 无论是外交政策、移民、贸易，还是宪政政府的规范。

sentences.en: Now, a majority or near majority of Americans will elect someone who potentially in the most radical ways will try and overturn that consensus.
sentences.zh: 现在，多数或接近多数的美国人将选出这样一个人，他可能会以最激进的方式试图颠覆这一共识。

sentences.en: Nate, just how much of a victory does this appear to be for Trump?
sentences.zh: 内特，这对于特朗普来说到底算是一场多大的胜利？

sentences.en: How close was this?
sentences.zh: 这场选举有多胶着？

sentences.en: By most measures, it's still going to be a fairly close election.
sentences.zh: 从大多数标准来看，这仍然会是一场相当接近的选举。

sentences.en: It should be noted he is favored to win the popular vote, which is extraordinary given that he lost the last two times, that no Republican has won it in 20 years.
sentences.zh: 应该指出的是，他有望赢得普选票，考虑到他前两次都输了，而且20年来没有共和党人赢得过普选票，这非常了不起。

sentences.en: But he may only win it by a point or two.
sentences.zh: 但他可能只赢一两个百分点。

sentences.en: Biden won it by four and a half, and we didn't consider that to be a landslide.
sentences.zh: 拜登赢了四个半百分点，而我们当时并不认为那是压倒性胜利。

sentences.en: He's probably going to sweep all of the swing states, but that would put him just over 300 electoral votes, not 370 like Obama.
sentences.zh: 他可能会横扫所有的摇摆州，但这只会让他获得刚过300张选举人票，而不是像奥巴马那样拿到370张。

sentences.en: So you can't call it a landslide,
sentences.zh: 所以你不能称之为压倒性胜利，

sentences.en: but it's a clear victory.
sentences.zh: 但这是一场清晰的胜利。

sentences.en: Okay, I want to talk about how Trump pulled this off.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想谈谈特朗普是如何做到这一点的。

sentences.en: And Nate, I want to stick with you because you were on the show yesterday
sentences.zh: 内特，我想继续听你的，因为你昨天就在节目中

sentences.en: outlining various scenarios for the outcome of this race.
sentences.zh: 概述了这次竞选结果的各种设想。

sentences.en: And the one that appears to have played out is what you identified as, and correct me if I'm wrong, the Trump realignment scenario.
sentences.zh: 而现在似乎上演的结果，正是你所指出的——如果我错了请纠正我——特朗普重组阵营的设想。

sentences.en: A pretty significant set of gains that extend and you could argue complete this populist revolution that he began back in 2016.
sentences.zh: 这是一套相当可观的收益，它延伸并可以说完成了他在2016年开始的那场民粹主义革命。

sentences.en: When I look at the map on the Times homepage that shows the differences between 2020 and tonight, it actually seems in a way to be bigger than that what Trump did
sentences.zh: 当我看着《纽约时报》主页上显示2020年与今晚之间差异的地图时，特朗普所做的事情在某种程度上似乎比那还要宏大，

sentences.en: because that map shows that between those two elections, the country moved right, it would seem, across the board.
sentences.zh: 因为那张地图显示，在这两次选举之间，整个国家似乎全面向右转了。

sentences.en: And on top of that, that map shows pretty much nothing broke Kamala Harris's way.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，那张地图显示几乎没有什么对卡玛拉·哈里斯有利的发展。

sentences.en: How did that happen based on what we know so far from the data?
sentences.zh: 根据我们目前从数据中了解到的情况，这是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: On a spectrum between a close 2020 repeat and a realignment, I would put it somewhere in the middle.
sentences.zh: 在2020年结果的简单重演与阵营重组之间的光谱上，我会把它放在中间某个位置。

sentences.en: But yes, this is a decisive victory and it's noteworthy that it was very broad.
sentences.zh: 但是的，这是一场决定性的胜利，而且值得注意的是，它的范围非常广泛。

sentences.en: There are very few parts of the country where Harris ran as well as Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 在全国很少有地方哈里斯的表现能赶上乔·拜登。

sentences.en: There are very few demographic groups where Harris ran as well as Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 在很少有人口群体中哈里斯的表现能赶上乔·拜登。

sentences.en: There were places that are traditionally liberal that swung, conservative places,
sentences.zh: 有些传统上自由派的地方发生了摇摆，保守派的地方也是如此，

sentences.en: Hispanic places, white working class.
sentences.zh: 拉美裔聚居区，白人工人阶级。

sentences.en: Every kind of county swung towards Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 各种类型的县都在向唐纳德·特朗普倾斜。

sentences.en: That says a lot about the deep-seated revulsion that was being expressed here at the status quo.
sentences.zh: 这充分说明了这里正在表达的对现状根深蒂固的厌恶。

sentences.en: This is very different to me than 2016 where there was this narrow Trump breakthrough among white college graduates that let him get over the top
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这与2016年有很大不同，当时特朗普在白人大学毕业生中实现了微小的突破，使他以微弱优势

sentences.en: in the critical Midwestern battleground states by a hair.
sentences.zh: 在关键的中西部战场州涉险过关。

sentences.en: This is a much more comfortable and broadly based victory.
sentences.zh: 这是一场更加游刃有余、基础更加广泛的胜利。

sentences.en: And I do think it counts as the culmination of the sort of broader Trump era of elections.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为这算得上更广泛的特朗普时代选举的高潮。

sentences.en: You know, he started in 2016 with this narrow breakthrough and now he has extended what had been a narrow coalition to something that is, you know, hardly,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他在2016年以这种微小的突破起步，现在他已经将原本狭窄的联盟扩大到了某种程度上，

sentences.en: we're still, again, talking about a relatively modest victory, but one that is still fundamentally much more broadly based than it once was.
sentences.zh: 我们依然在讨论一场相对温和的胜利，但它在根本上比以前广泛得多。

sentences.en: And again, we've now changed what American politics is about in some way.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我们现在某种程度上改变了美国政治的内涵。

sentences.en: We have a new political division in the country
sentences.zh: 我们在国内有了一种新的政治分歧，

sentences.en: and there are a lot of different people in demographic groups that previously did not support Donald Trump who appear to be receptive to different elements of that message.
sentences.zh: 并且有许多不同的人和人口群体，他们以前不支持唐纳德·特朗普，现在似乎对该信息的不同要素持接受态度。

sentences.en: Can you just explain what you mean when you say we're never going back?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下你说的“我们再也回不去了”是什么意思吗？

sentences.en: I think there's definitely a political realignment.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是一场政治重组。

sentences.en: You know, for a long time, we had this sort of Obama era of politics where demographics would be destiny and a more diversifying nation would definitely go towards Democrats
sentences.zh: 你知道的，很长一段时间里，我们有这种奥巴马时代的政治，即人口结构就是命运，一个日益多元化的国家肯定会倒向民主党，

sentences.en: and that was the belief.
sentences.zh: 当时大家就是这样深信不疑的。

sentences.en: And we're seeing, granted it's still early, that that is not what's necessarily going to happen.
sentences.zh: 而我们现在看到的是，尽管现在还为时尚早，但这并不一定会发生。

sentences.en: It might, something very different appears to be happening.
sentences.zh: 也许会发生，但目前出现的情况似乎大不相同。

sentences.en: And so we're entering, I sort of see it as ending one political era in terms of the politics and entering another one.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正在进入——我将其视为在政治层面上结束一个政治时代，并进入另一个时代。

sentences.en: But I think there's like a larger, slightly more philosophical question as well, which is there was this sense that Trump was an aberration in some way,
sentences.zh: 但我也认为还有一个更宏大、稍微更具哲学性的问题，那就是曾经有一种感觉，即特朗普在某种程度上是个反常现象，

sentences.en: that he was a deviation from American politics and his term and his win was a deviation.
sentences.zh: 他是美国政治的一个偏差，他的任期和胜利是一个偏差。

sentences.en: And all these things he did, be it, you know, stoking January 6th or refusing to accept the results of the 2020 election or even just how he talked about people,
sentences.zh: 而他所做的所有事情，无论是煽动1月6日事件，还是拒绝接受2020年选举结果，甚至只是他谈论人们的方式，

sentences.en: those things are not an aberration in our politics.
sentences.zh: 这些事情在我们政治中已经不再是反常现象了。

sentences.en: Those things are our politics now.
sentences.zh: 这些事情现在就是我们的政治。

sentences.en: And that's where I think the country is.
sentences.zh: 这就是我认为目前国家所处的状态。

sentences.en: And that, I think, is what a lot of people, probably tomorrow morning, are going to have to confront.
sentences.zh: 而我认为，这正是明天早晨许多人不得不直面的现实。

sentences.en: Nate, you just mentioned how much success
sentences.zh: 内特，你刚才提到唐纳德·特朗普

sentences.en: Donald Trump had with a variety of voting blocs that, as Lisa, you just pointed out,
sentences.zh: 在各个选民群体中取得了多大的成功，正如丽莎你刚才指出的那样，

sentences.en: Democrats had long believed were going to remain loyal to them.
sentences.zh: 民主党人长期以来一直相信这些群体会忠于他们。

sentences.en: And, but why?
sentences.zh: 但是，为什么呢？

sentences.en: But why?
sentences.zh: 但是，为什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why did they believe that?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么会那样相信？

sentences.en: Like, that evidence has been clear about the drop-off for a long time, right?
sentences.zh: 就像，长期以来支持率下降的证据一直很明显，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, we've had 2016, we've had 2020.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们经历了2016年，我们经历了2020年。

sentences.en: Like, we've actually had a lot of evidence to say that the demographic destiny undertone is one that is a faulty premise.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们实际上有大量的证据表明，人口结构决定命运的潜台词是一个错误的假设。

sentences.en: The fact that they are holding on to the Obama era, in my opinion, is a racist assumption.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，他们紧抓奥巴马时代不放，是一种带有种族色彩的假设。

sentences.en: I don't mean it like in a capital R way, but I mean it in-
sentences.zh: 我不是指大写 R 那种意味，我的意思是——

sentences.en: It's a race-based assumption.
sentences.zh: 这是一个基于种族的假设。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's, I would say, lowercase raciSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为，我会说这是小写的种族主义。

sentences.en: I would say that there is an assumption that this, it was a failure of imagination, that it couldn't be true.
sentences.zh: 我会说存在这样一种假设，即这是一种想象力的失败，人们无法相信这是真的。

sentences.en: I hear you.
sentences.zh: 我明白你的意思。

sentences.en: But I think there is a sense of like, yes, we saw this drumbeat coming.
sentences.zh: 但我认为有一种感觉，那就是，是的，我们看到了这股声势的到来。

sentences.en: We saw that more people were identifying as Republicans in like all these polls.
sentences.zh: 我们看到在所有这些民调中，有更多的人认同自己是共和党人。

sentences.en: We saw that Democrats had moved towards the more conservative position on issues like immigration.
sentences.zh: 我们看到民主党人在移民等问题上已经转向了更保守的立场。

sentences.en: We saw that representation did not motivate people of color.
sentences.zh: 我们看到代表性并没有激励有色人种。

sentences.en: We saw that, yeah, that's, you know, representation isn't enough.
sentences.zh: 我们看到，是的，你知道的，仅仅有代表性是不够的。

sentences.en: But at the same time-
sentences.zh: 但与此同时——

sentences.en: You're saying having a black candidate.
sentences.zh: 你是说推出一位黑人候选人。

sentences.en: Yeah, people don't vote just on representation.
sentences.zh: 是的，人们不会仅仅为了代表性而投票。

sentences.en: There's another half of this, though, which is that Democrats lost sight of why they were winning voters like this in the first place.
sentences.zh: 不过，这里还有另一个关键因素，那就是民主党人忽视了他们当初赢得这些选民的原因。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Preach.
sentences.zh: 说得好。

sentences.en: Which is?
sentences.zh: 是什么原因？

sentences.en: Well, one reason that I think is worth mentioning is the economy and helping working people against the establishment and corporations.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为值得一提的一个原因就是经济，以及帮助劳动人民对抗建制派和大公司。

sentences.en: It was the Democrats who used to be the party that was advocating change, that was against the establishment, that could channel the, you know,
sentences.zh: 过去正是民主党人标榜自己是倡导变革的政党，是反对建制派的政党，能够引导……

sentences.en: emotions of a disaffected young person.
sentences.zh: 那些心怀不满的年轻人的情绪。

sentences.en: Donald Trump is that candidate.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普就是那样的候选人。

sentences.en: And so they should in no way be surprised that they have lost those people.
sentences.zh: 所以他们失去这些人，绝对不应该感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I just want to make sure I understand what I think you're all hinting at, which is that Donald Trump and the Republican Party have completed a journey
sentences.zh: 我只是想确保我理解了你们所有人都在暗示的意思，那就是唐纳德·特朗普和共和党已经完成了一段旅程，

sentences.en: in which they are the party of disruption.
sentences.zh: 在这段旅程中，他们成为了代表颠覆的政党。

sentences.en: They are the party that assaults the establishment.
sentences.zh: 他们是冲击建制派的政党。

sentences.en: They are the party that says, not just to the white working class, but to the working class in a number of different demographic groups,
sentences.zh: 他们是一个不仅对白人工人阶级，而且对许多不同族裔群体的工人阶级说——

sentences.en: including black and Latino working class Americans, that we are your refuge from an unfair, broken system.
sentences.zh: 包括黑人和拉丁裔美国工人阶级——我们是你们在不公、破碎系统中的避难所的政党。

sentences.en: And I would only add that their ability to do that was made easier by a Democratic Party who ceded the mantle on that front.
sentences.zh: 我只想补充一点，民主党人在这一阵地让出了领导权，这使得他们能够更容易地做到这一点。

sentences.en: The biggest character in this race, to me, was not on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这场竞选中最大的人物并没有出现在选票上。

sentences.en: It was Joe Biden, in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，那就是乔·拜登。

sentences.en: Like, Joe Biden's refusal to do what he has implied he would do in 2020 and transition to a different type of generation, allow Democrats to have a broader conversation
sentences.zh: 比如，乔·拜登拒绝兑现他在2020年暗示过的事，即实现向不同代际的过渡，允许民主党人就

sentences.en: about change, allow Democrats to be freed from the status quo, is not what happened.
sentences.zh: 变革展开更广泛的讨论，允许民主党人从现状中解脱出来，但这并没有发生。

sentences.en: I think it would be easier for me to say that Donald Trump completed this mass realignment among the working class if we had a universe where the Democrats had a primary,
sentences.zh: 如果民主党人进行了一场初选，且我们处在一个这样的世界中——

sentences.en: where the Democrats nominated a candidate that was based around some set of ideas, and it was not tied to this administration so clearly, and the status quo.
sentences.zh: 在这个世界里，民主党人提名的候选人基于某种理念，并且没有与现政府及现状如此清晰地绑定在一起，那么我认为要说唐纳德·特朗普完成了工人阶级的这次大洗牌，对我来说会容易一些。

sentences.en: But since that is not what happened,
sentences.zh: 但既然事实并非如此，

sentences.en: I think it has made the Republican ability to be the agents of change so much easier that I find it the biggest thing that has happened in this race,
sentences.zh: 我认为这让共和党人充当变革推动者变得容易得多，以至于我认为这是这场竞选发生的最重大事情，

sentences.en: and I think speaks to what we're saying about what's happened over the last three months.
sentences.zh: 并且我认为这也说明了我们刚才所说的过去三个月发生的事情。

sentences.en: The place that they were in before the candidate switch happened made it such that you could run a perfect race or whatever.
sentences.zh: 在候选人更替发生之前他们所处的位置，使得你无论怎么做也只能打出一场完美的选战。

sentences.en: And you are still playing on the ground that brings you to 50-50.
sentences.zh: 而你依然是在将你拉回五五开的格局中竞争。

sentences.en: Because the biggest thing, in my opinion, that happened was they tied themselves to an unpopular administration and with it, the status quo.
sentences.zh: 因为在我看来，最重要的事情是，他们把自己和一个不受欢迎的政府以及与之相伴的现状绑在了一起。

sentences.en: That did not represent change.
sentences.zh: 这并不代表变革。

sentences.en: And there was a lot of evidence that that was a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 有大量证据表明这是一个糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: I want to turn to what happened with women in tonight's election.
sentences.zh: 我想转向今晚选举中女性群体的情况。

sentences.en: It seemed, despite everything we're talking about here, like the Harris campaign was relying on women to save the Democratic coalition.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们在这里讨论了这一切，但哈里斯的竞选团队似乎仍寄希望于女性来拯救民主党联盟。

sentences.en: And the view was suburban women, even moderate Republican women, post the overturning of Roe v.
sentences.zh: 当时的观点是，在罗诉韦德案被推翻之后，

sentences.en: Wade, and given all of Donald Trump's character flaws, was going to put Kamala Harris over the edge, despite the fact that perhaps she didn't speak to and embody change in the way
sentences.zh: 且鉴于唐纳德·特朗普身上所有的性格瑕疵，郊区女性，甚至是温和派共和党女性，将会把卡玛拉·哈里斯推向胜利，尽管她可能并没有以

sentences.en: that so many other Americans wanted.
sentences.zh: 许多其他美国人所期望的方式去讲述和体现变革。

sentences.en: Did those women not show up?
sentences.zh: 难道这些女性没有出来投票吗？

sentences.en: Or did they show up?
sentences.zh: 还是说她们出来了？

sentences.en: But it didn't matter because of all the other voters who showed up for Trump.
sentences.zh: 但由于所有其他为特朗普投票的选民，这一切都变得无关紧要了。

sentences.en: So it's a little hard to say at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以目前很难说清楚。

sentences.en: Like, men and women live together in all precincts, it turns out.
sentences.zh: 毕竟事实证明，男人和女人在所有选区都是生活在一起的。

sentences.en: So it's a little hard to separate that out.
sentences.zh: 因此很难将这些因素完全剥离开来。

sentences.en: I do think we can say something about the power of abortion rights, you know, since Dobbs in 2022, that had been such a motivator for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 不过我认为我们可以谈谈堕胎权的力量，你知道的，自2022年多布斯案以来，这一直是民主党人的强大动力。

sentences.en: And I think now, maybe even because of all the state referendums, you had a sense that voters could support both abortion rights and former President Trump.
sentences.zh: 而且我想现在，也许正是因为所有的州级公投，你会感觉到选民既能支持堕胎权，也能支持前总统特朗普。

sentences.en: And that was different than what we had seen in the 2022 midterMs.
sentences.zh: 这与我们在2022年中期选举中看到的情况有所不同。

sentences.en: So I wonder if the power of that issue was a little diminished in some way.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，这个议题的力量在某种程度上是否有所减弱。

sentences.en: That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有意思。

sentences.en: I would also only add, like, and this is anecdotal, of course, but a lot of folks we met in our travels understood Donald Trump as having a different position on abortion
sentences.zh: 我还要补充一点，虽然这当然是个别现象，但我们在各地走访时遇到的很多人认为，唐纳德·特朗普在堕胎问题上的立场

sentences.en: than the rest of the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 与共和党其他成员不同。

sentences.en: Yes, yeah, that's definitely true.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错，这绝对是真的。

sentences.en: And one thing that Donald Trump...
sentences.zh: 而唐纳德·特朗普有一点...

sentences.en: Can you just explain that?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: In the last year and a half, he's created distance from the most evangelical wing of Republicans.
sentences.zh: 在过去一年半里，他一直在与共和党内最激进的福音派翼保持距离。

sentences.en: He has upset some of them.
sentences.zh: 他惹恼了其中一些人。

sentences.en: And I think we have to acknowledge, I think some of that worked, frankly.
sentences.zh: 我想我们必须承认，坦白说，其中一些策略确实起作用了。

sentences.en: In other words, people did not buy the idea that he was a true believer in the opposition to abortion.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，人们并不买账他真的是个坚定的反堕胎信徒这一说法。

sentences.en: I guess I'm not saying that.
sentences.zh: 我想我不是在说这个。

sentences.en: Yeah, they never have.
sentences.zh: 对，他们从来没这么想过。

sentences.en: I'm just saying, like...
sentences.zh: 我只是在说，比如...

sentences.en: They never have believed that.
sentences.zh: 他们从来没相信过这一点。

sentences.en: The idea that abortion had to be placed top of your list
sentences.zh: 那种认为必须把堕胎放在你清单首位的想法

sentences.en: because Republicans represented an existential threat to that right,
sentences.zh: ——因为共和党人对这一权利构成了生存威胁——

sentences.en: I have had people articulate to me how that does not apply to Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 曾有人向我清晰地表达过这并不适用于唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: People have mentioned consistently that Donald Trump is different than other Republicans on abortion rights.
sentences.zh: 人们一直提到，在堕胎权问题上，唐纳德·特朗普与其他共和党人不同。

sentences.en: Now, I would also say that I think there is some failure of imagination on behalf of voters about Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 不过，我也想说，我认为选民在对唐纳德·特朗普的想象力方面存在某种缺失。

sentences.en: Like, I think that you can...
sentences.zh: 比如，我认为你可以...

sentences.en: That folks can have that feeling and it not be true, right?
sentences.zh: 人们可以有这种感觉，但这并不是真的，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, he's still wrapped up in a conservative ecosystem that is anti-abortion.
sentences.zh: 比如，他依然深陷于反堕胎的保守派生态系统中。

sentences.en: I just think we have to acknowledge, since we're talking about gender, that in two of the last three presidential races, is a woman running against Donald Trump loSt.
sentences.zh: 既然我们在谈论性别，我认为我们必须承认，在过去三场总统大选中，有两场是女性与唐纳德·特朗普竞选并落败。

sentences.en: This race meant a lot, as Hillary Clinton's campaign against Trump meant a lot to women.
sentences.zh: 这场竞选意义重大，正如希拉里·克林顿对阵特朗普的竞选对女性意义重大一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I wonder what happens now, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，我想知道接下来会发生什么，对吧？

sentences.en: What we saw in 2016 was, obviously, the Women's March and everyone got out with their hats and then you saw this flourishing of the Me Too movement that prompted this really
sentences.zh: 我们在2016年看到的是，显然有“女性大游行”，每个人都戴着帽子走上街头，随后你便看到了“我也是”运动的蓬勃发展，这引发了关于性别和性别平等的

sentences.en: public and private reckoning around gender and gender equity.
sentences.zh: 真正公开和私下的深刻反思。

sentences.en: And then you saw all these women run and succeed.
sentences.zh: 然后你看到所有这些女性参选并成功。

sentences.en: You know, in 2018, you had record-breaking numbers of women elected to Congress.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在2018年，创纪录数量的女性当选国会议员。

sentences.en: In 2019, you had six women in unprecedented number run for the presidency.
sentences.zh: 在2019年，有数量空前的六位女性参加总统竞选。

sentences.en: So much so that Biden, you know, promised to pick a woman.
sentences.zh: 以至于拜登承诺要挑选一名女性。

sentences.en: He selected Harris and put her in as vice president.
sentences.zh: 他选择了哈里斯并让她担任副总统。

sentences.en: And now, after all of that, this movement that seemed like it was building towards the White House, in fact, it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 而现在，在经历这一切之后，这个似乎正朝着白宫迈进的运动，实际上并没有成功。

sentences.en: And I just don't think anyone's going to be out marching with their little pink hats this time around.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这次不会再有人戴着他们的小粉帽出去游行了。

sentences.en: I think the reaction will be something different, but I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我认为反应会有所不同，但我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know what it will be.
sentences.zh: 我不知道会是什么样的反应。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: This is one of the best questions about what happens next is what is the visceral emotional response from what eight years ago was called the resistance.
sentences.zh: 关于接下来会发生什么，最好的问题之一就是：对于八年前被称为“抵抗运动”的群体，将会产生怎样的本能情绪反应？

sentences.en: But broadly speaking,
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，

sentences.en: from liberals and college graduates, the sort of groups that have powered
sentences.zh: 从自由派和大学毕业生，也就是那些推动了

sentences.en: Democratic successes in midterms and special elections,
sentences.zh: 民主党在中期选举和特别选举中获胜的群体来看，

sentences.en: I personally don't see how it could be the same.
sentences.zh: 我个人看不出怎么可能会和以前一样。

sentences.en: having him win again and like this is going to hit very differently.
sentences.zh: 看到他再次获胜，这种冲击感将会截然不同。

sentences.en: And there's also a sort of natural exhaustion, I think, to this sort of response to Trump over time that I felt, I personally thought I observed in this campaign
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，随着时间推移，这种针对特朗普的反应本身也带有一种自然的疲惫感，我个人觉得我在这次竞选中观察到了这一点，

sentences.en: and it was reflected in the data as well in terms of lower voter registration and so on.
sentences.zh: 并且从选民登记率下降等数据中也能反映出来。

sentences.en: I don't know what will be the reaction in an emotional way for the Democratic activist rank and file.
sentences.zh: 我不知道民主党基层激进分子会在情感上有何反应。

sentences.en: We're going to take a very quick break and we're going to try to stay on schedule,
sentences.zh: 我们要进行一个非常简短的休息，我们要尽量按计划进行，

sentences.en: Nate, so you can get back to the needle.
sentences.zh: 内特，这样你就能回到那个仪表盘前了。

sentences.en: So we'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game
sentences.zh: 我编写了“连连看”游戏，

sentences.en: Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 这是《纽约时报》游戏中的一个字谜，我非常喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky and I create the game
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天都负责创作

sentences.en: Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis and I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: “拼写蜜蜂”和“字母包”游戏，我有一种叫做色听觉的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由刚才你们听到声音的这些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: I think we need to wrestle with some of the realities of Donald Trump's weaknesses and Nate, whenever we've talked to you in the past, you spoke of whether it was
sentences.zh: 我认为我们需要正视唐纳德·特朗普的某些弱点所带来的现实。内特，每当我们在过去与你交谈时，你都会提到——

sentences.en: Trump's rule on January 6th, his convictions in the hush money scheme, not to mention the tax fraud, his increasingly racist, race-baiting rhetoric, which we really saw at the end
sentences.zh: 无论是特朗普在1月6日的行径、他在封口费案中的定罪，更不用说税务欺诈，以及他日益严重的种族主义、煽动种族仇恨的言论（我们在本次竞选结束时的一些集会上确实看到了这一点）——

sentences.en: of this campaign at some of his rallies, as his single biggest vulnerabilities.
sentences.zh: 这些都是他最大的单一软肋。

sentences.en: And I want to understand in your mind if a victory here means that voters were looking past those things or if, as in 2016, but obviously the facts on the ground are different,
sentences.zh: 我想了解在你的心目中，如果这里出现一场胜利，是否意味着选民选择忽略了这些事情，或者说，正如2016年那样（尽管现实情况有所不同），

sentences.en: we need to see this as part of the appeal of what voters liked about Donald Trump this time around.
sentences.zh: 我们应当将此视为选民这次喜欢唐纳德·特朗普的原因的一部分。

sentences.en: I think that voters have never liked
sentences.zh: 我认为选民从来都没有喜欢过

sentences.en: Donald Trump, but I have to say he's a lot more popular today than he was in 2016.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普，但我必须说，他今天比2016年受欢迎得多。

sentences.en: In 2016, you know, his unfavorable rating was like, rather his favorable rating was like 30%,
sentences.zh: 在2016年，你知道的，他的反感率大约是，或者说他的好感率大约是30%，

sentences.en: Now it's close to 50%.
sentences.zh: 现在接近50%了。

sentences.en: A lot of people who didn't like him eight years ago, they've come around to him.
sentences.zh: 很多八年前不喜欢他的人，现在都转而支持他了。

sentences.en: That is partly because I think he ran a much more disciplined campaign than he did eight years ago.
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为我认为他这次的竞选比八年前纪律严明得多。

sentences.en: I think it's partly because he's become normalized for lack of a better word.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是因为，换个更好的词来说，他已经变得正常化了。

sentences.en: He's something we're all accustomed to and he has positive attributes as well, whether it's his perceived economic stewardship or that people think he's funny and so on
sentences.zh: 他成了我们都习以为常的事物，而且他也有积极的特质，无论是他被认为具有经济管理能力，还是人们觉得他很有趣等等，

sentences.en: and that he's not politically correct and those combination of things can lead someone to come around to him and look past his liabilities.
sentences.zh: 并且他不搞政治正确，这些因素结合起来就会导致某人转而支持他并忽视他的劣势。

sentences.en: That said, I still don't think that on net
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我仍然认为从净效应来看，

sentences.en: Trump is a strong candidate.
sentences.zh: 特朗普并不是一个强有力的候选人。

sentences.en: I think that the balance of his strengths and weaknesses at best cancel out and may well be on net worse than a different
sentences.zh: 我认为他优势与劣势的权衡充其量只是互相抵消，并且净效应很可能比换作另一个

sentences.en: Republican candidate.
sentences.zh: 共和党候选人还要糟糕。

sentences.en: That's not to say they would have won in the same way, but I do think that Republicans have probably left votes on the table by having Donald Trump as their frontrunner
sentences.zh: 这并不是说他们会以同样的方式获胜，但我确实认为，共和党人让唐纳德·特朗普担任领头羊，可能在无形中流失了选票，

sentences.en: even though someone like Donald Trump is the only person who could have turned the Republican
sentences.zh: 尽管像唐纳德·特朗普这样的人是唯一能将共和党

sentences.en: Party into what it has become.
